title: minimize-host-interrupts-and-thread-parking-in-copy-path
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Host-side overhead during prefill->decode handoff is dominated by frequent short memcopies, syscall wakeups, and thread parking/unparking that amplify 95th/99th latency spikes under bursty request patterns. This ticket targets reduction of interrupts and thread parking in the host copy path while preserving correctness across heterogeneous GPU types.

Goals: (1) reduce 95th-percentile prefill latency by >=20% for realistic chat workloads; (2) reduce CPU steal/consumption on prefill host threads by >=25% during peak; (3) avoid increasing tail latency on long sequences; (4) maintain memory safety and multi-tenant isolation.

Proposed approach:
- Introduce a long-lived pinned-buffer pool per NUMA node with small fixed-size segments tuned to token-batch distributions to avoid repeated pin/unpin and reduce page faults.
- Replace short-lived condition-variable parking with hybrid adaptive-spin SPSC handoff queues for hot producer-consumer pairs (host prefill writer -> GPU DMA thread) and fall back to eventfd-based batching for lower-frequency paths.
- Batch eventfd/syscall wakeups by coalescing completion notifications in micro-batches (configurable timeframe, default 250us) to amortize syscall cost while keeping latency SLOs.
- Add a lightweight zero-copy descriptor that points into pinned pool regions so we avoid memcpy when sequence fits segment size; when larger, use a two-stage copy to pinned staging buffer to keep DMA path streamlined.
- Introduce a tunable "spin-budget" per worker thread (experimentally 10-50us) with a progressive backoff to avoid wasted CPU on long stalls.
- Kernel-selection tie-in: expose a runtime hint so the kernel picker can prefer attention kernels tolerant of slightly higher jitter when using larger batching / coalescing.

Acceptance criteria (measured on dedicated 4xA100 dev rig and on hosted canary):
- 95th-percentile end-to-end prefill latency improvement >= 20% on chat-sim workload (token length distribution attached).
- Host-side CPU utilization during 95th/99th tail drops >= 25% on the same workload.
- No increase >5% in token error/retry rates for model runs.
- Feature gated and can be disabled per-customer or route via config.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Coalescing wakeups increases median latency slightly for the coldest, lowest-volume requests; mitigated by short coalesce windows and per-route overrides.
- Pinned buffer pool increases resident memory footprint; mitigated by per-GPU quota and segment reclamation after idle windows.
- Adaptive spinning may waste CPU if misconfigured on noisy multitenant hosts; we will auto-tune spin budgets in later iteration.

Measurement plan:
- Add perf counters for syscalls/sec (eventfd, futex), memcpy bytes/sec, average spin time, and pinned pool hit-rate.
- Benchmarks: chat-sim (50k requests, mixed lengths), heavy-prefill (long sequences, 4x concurrency), and synthetic spike tests (short bursts).
- Dashboards: link to Grafana panel for host copy path latency and kernel decision impact.

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Host+Interrupt+Reduction+Design
- Initial perf run (before/after): https://grafana.redwood-infra.com/d/abcd/host-copy-comparison
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Instrumentation and metrics (2d): add counters and lightweight tracing spans for memcopy and wake-up paths.
2) Pinned pool + zero-copy descriptor (3d): implement pool with eviction policy and tests.
3) Adaptive-spin SPSC queue (4d): hot-path replacement for writer->dma thread.
4) Eventfd batching layer and config UI toggle (3d): coalesce notifications and expose route-level controls.
5) Canary rollout and measurement (4d): staged canary on runtime-1.22, monitor metrics, rollback plan.

Follow-ups (separate tickets): auto-tune spin-budget, per-customer memory caps for pinned pool, integrate with Dedicated autoscaler policies.
comments: 2025-11-12 Ayesha Patel: Created ticket after spike analysis showed >40% syscall overhead in host copy path during afternoon traffic spikes. Attached perf flamegraphs and traces.

2025-11-18 Luca Moretti: Prototype SPSC queue implemented. Microbenchmarks show 18% reduction in syscall rate and 9% drop in 95th prefill latency on dev rig. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456

2025-11-22 Performance team: After adding pinned buffer pool, pinned-hit rate is 72% in baseline runs; end-to-end 95th latency now at -22% vs baseline. Observed memory resident increase of ~120MB on 4xA100 node.

2025-11-27 Ops: Canary run started on canary cluster (runtime-1.22-canary). Monitoring for multi-tenant interference; setting initial spin-budget to 20us. No regressions observed in token error rates so far.
2025-12-03 Luca Moretti: Implemented eventfd coalescing and route-level toggle UI. Preparing rollout notes and rollback steps. Next: perf regression sweep and documentation for SREs.
